You are verifying a Node.js (ESM, .mjs) port of a Python script.

REFERENCE (ground truth, run it, do NOT modify):
  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a <hrp> --b <witver> --c <comma-separated ints>
  Source: /workspace/dataset/test4.py  (argparse: --a str required, --b int required, --c str required;
  witprog = list(map(int, args.c.split(','))); result = bech32.encode(args.a, args.b, witprog); print(result))
  The bundled Python "bech32" package internals are NOT viewable - treat it as a black box.

PORT UNDER TEST (read it, do NOT edit it):
  /output/test4.mjs  plus  /output/lib/py/*.mjs  and  /output/lib/bech32/*.mjs
  Run as: node /output/test4.mjs --a bc --b 5 --c 1,2,3

DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS (already written, use it):
  /tmp/difftest.mjs exports  runAll(cases, {label})  where cases is an array of argv arrays.
  It compares stdout, stderr (with [PYI-<pid>:ERROR] normalized) and exit code, and prints
  "[label] pass=N/M fail=K" followed by up to 20 MISMATCH blocks.
  Write your own generator script in /tmp/<yourname>.mjs like:
    import { runAll } from '/tmp/difftest.mjs';
    const cases = [ ['--a','bc','--b','5','--c','1,2'], ... ];
    await runAll(cases, { label: 'mycat' });
  Set env DIFF_CONCURRENCY=6 when running (e.g. DIFF_CONCURRENCY=6 node /tmp/mine.mjs) to avoid
  thrashing, and keep each run under ~800 cases so it finishes in a couple of minutes. Split into
  several runs if you need more coverage. Every process pair costs ~120ms of wall clock.

RULES:
 - NEVER edit anything under /output. Report only. Another process applies fixes.
 - A finding counts ONLY if you actually ran both binaries and observed a difference in
   stdout, exit code, or (PID-normalized) stderr. Paste the exact argv and both observed outputs.
 - Differences purely in the PyInstaller PID number are NOT findings.
 - Report the shortest reproducing argv you can find.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (mainstream):
Fuzz the MAINSTREAM success path. Random realistic inputs: hrp drawn from lowercase
letters/digits of length 1..12 (e.g. bc, tb, ltc, test, doge, x9), witness version 0..16,
witness program of random length 2..40 with random bytes 0..255. Generate at least 600 random
cases across two runs plus these deliberate boundaries: witver 0 with program length exactly
19, 20, 21, 31, 32, 33; witver 1..16 with lengths 2, 3, 20, 32, 39, 40, 41. Confirm the port
agrees on both the encoded address and on which inputs print "None".

import argparse
import bech32

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--a", type=str, required=True)  # HRP
    parser.add_argument("--b", type=int, required=True)  # Witness version
    parser.add_argument("--c", type=str, required=True)  # Witness program as comma-separated integers
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    witprog = list(map(int, args.c.split(',')))
    result = bech32.encode(args.a, args.b, witprog)  # Encode segwit address
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
No mismatches found. Summary of what I ran:

**Differential batches (all pass, 0 fail):**
- `/tmp/mainstream_bounds.mjs` — 368/368. The required boundaries: witver 0 with program lengths 19/20/21/31/32/33 across 6 hrps; witver 1..16 with lengths 2/3/20/32/39/40/41 across 2 hrps; full length sweep 1..42 for witver 0 and 16; all-zero and all-255 programs.
- `/tmp/mainstream_rand.mjs` — 400/400 (SEED=12345) and 400/400 (SEED=987654321). Random hrp from `[a-z0-9]{1,12}`, witver 0..16, program length 2..40, bytes 0..255.
- `/tmp/mainstream_sweep.mjs` — 663/663. Dense cross product witver 0..16 × length 2..40 with random bytes.
- `/tmp/mainstream_hrp.mjs` — 396/396. 33 hrp shapes including ones that contain the `1` separator character (`1`, `11`, `a1`, `1a`, `a1b`, `bc1`, `abc1def`, `l1l`), all-digit hrps, single-char hrps, and 12-char hrps.
- `/tmp/mainstream_fmt.mjs` — 166/166. `int()`-accepted decorations on the program bytes and on witver (leading/trailing spaces, tabs/newlines, `+`, zero padding).

**Both branches genuinely exercised.** Verified directly against the reference that witver 0 yields an address only at lengths 20 and 32 (19/21/33/40/41 and length 2 all print `None`), witver 1..16 yields an address for lengths 2..40 and `None` at 41, and the port agrees on every one of those classifications.

**Two read-based suspicions I chased and disproved** (worth recording so nobody "fixes" them):
1. `/output/lib/bech32/codec.mjs:36` omits CPython `bech32_decode`'s `len(bech) > 90` guard. The bundled package has no such cap either — `--a aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --b 1 --c <forty 1s>` produces a 91-char address from both, and hrps up to length 80 produce 152-char addresses identically. Not a bug.
2. `/output/lib/bech32/segwit.mjs:41` returns `null` when `convertBits` fails, where stock `bech32` 1.1.0 would raise `TypeError` on `[witver] + None`. Reference on `--a bc --b 1 --c 256,1` prints `None` / rc=0, same as the port. The bundled encode has a `None` guard. Not a bug.
3. Also confirmed the port's core assumption in `/output/lib/bech32/segwit.mjs` — Bech32 checksum for *all* witness versions, no Bech32m — is correct: reference gives `bc1pqypqj3p230` for `--a bc --b 1 --c 1,2`, which is the plain-Bech32 checksum.

input.notes:
No mainstream-path differences found across 2393 harness case-pairs (5 further manual pairs run by hand). Coverage: (1) /tmp/mainstream_bounds.mjs 368/368 — every required boundary: witver 0 with program lengths 19,20,21,31,32,33 over 6 hrps ('bc','tb','test','x9','a','abcdefghijkl'); witver 1..16 with lengths 2,3,20,32,39,40,41 over 'bc' and 'ltc'; plus exhaustive length 1..42 for witver 0 and 16; plus all-0x00 and all-0xff programs at lengths 2,20,32,40 for witver 0,1,16. (2) /tmp/mainstream_rand.mjs 400/400 at SEED=12345 and 400/400 at SEED=987654321 — random hrp [a-z0-9]{1,12}, witver 0..16, program length 2..40, random bytes 0..255, with witver-0 cases biased so half hit valid length 20/32. (3) /tmp/mainstream_sweep.mjs 663/663 — dense cross product witver 0..16 x length 2..40, random bytes. (4) /tmp/mainstream_hrp.mjs 396/396 — 33 hrp shapes x 12 (witver,length) combos, deliberately including hrps that contain the '1' separator char ('1','11','a1','1a','a1b','bc1','q1q','1bc','abc1def','l1l'), all-digit hrps ('999','000000','0123456789ab'), 1-char and 12-char hrps. (5) /tmp/mainstream_fmt.mjs 166/166 — int()-accepted literal decorations on program bytes and on witver (leading/trailing space, tab/newline, '+' sign, zero padding).

Both output branches are genuinely exercised and agree: witver 0 produces an address only at program length 20 or 32 (2,19,21,33,40,41 -> "None"); witver 1..16 produces an address for lengths 2..40 and "None" at 41; witver order-of-operations (checksum computed before CHARSET lookup) needs witver>=32 to matter and is outside this assignment.

Two suspicions raised by reading the port, both CHASED AND DISPROVED — do not "fix" them: (a) /output/lib/bech32/codec.mjs:36 omits CPython bech32_decode's `len(bech) > 90` guard, but the bundled package has no cap either: `--a aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --b 1 --c <forty 1s>` yields the same 91-char address from both, and hrp lengths 19,25,30,31,40,60,80 all round-trip identically up to 152 chars. (b) /output/lib/bech32/segwit.mjs:41 returns null when convertBits fails, whereas stock bech32 1.1.0 would raise TypeError on `[witver] + None`; the reference prints "None" rc=0 for `--a bc --b 1 --c 256,1`, matching the port, so the bundled encode has its own None guard. Also independently confirmed the port's central assumption (plain Bech32 checksum for every witness version, no Bech32m): reference emits bc1pqypqj3p230 for `--a bc --b 1 --c 1,2`.

Nothing suspicious remains unconfirmed on the mainstream success path.
